problem: A math exam consists of $10$ questions, with each question containing four possible answers, where only one is the correct answer. Michael takes the exam and, for each question, he randomly chooses one of the four answers. What is the probability that Michael answers at least eight questions correctly? Round your answer to $4$ decimal places.

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Probability of a Binomial Random Variable Over an Interval
examples.problem: A standard fair die is rolled $8$ times. What is the probability of rolling an even number at least $7$ times? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
examples.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of times we get an even number.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=8$ rolls

- the probability of rolling an even number on any roll of the die is

$$
p=\dfrac{3}{6} = 0.5
$$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X\sim B(8,0.5).$ 

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x) = \binom{n}{x} p^x (1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{x})(0.5)^{x}(1-0.5)^{8-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{x})(0.5)^{x}(0.5)^{8-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability of rolling an even number at least $7$ times. So, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\ge 7) & =P(X=7)+P(X=8) \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{7})(0.5)^{7}(0.5)^{8-7}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{8})(0.5)^{8}(0.5)^{8-8} \\  & =8(0.5)^{7}(0.5)+1(0.5)^{8} \\  & =0.035\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

feedback.problem: The probability that John succeeds in selling an insurance policy to a given customer is $0.45.$ On a given day, he interacts with $8$ customers. Assuming that the transactions with each customer are independent, what is the probability that he will sell exactly $2$ insurance policies on this day? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
feedback.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of insurance policies that John sells on this day.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=8$ customers

- the probability that John succeeds in selling an insurance policy to a given customer is $p=0.45$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(8,0.45).$ We want to find the probability that he will sell exactly $2$ insurance policies.

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=2) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{8}{2})(0.45)^{2}(1-0.45)^{8-2} \\  & =\frac{8!}{2!(8-2)!}(0.45)^{2}(0.55)^{6} \\  & =28(0.45)^{2}(0.55)^{6} \\  & ≈0.157\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
